text:
mike: noticing a weird pattern on prod: clients doing fast reconnects after a 204 from the proxy, but console shows duplicate consumption/charge. anyone seen this?
anya: hmm, 204 from proxy? we expect SSE to stay open on 204 chunked responses. which proxy?
mike: the eu-edge proxy that does `X-Proxy-Keepalive: yes`. looks like the client treats the 204 as terminal, reconnects, and we double-bill tokens when resume succeeds.
shrey: can you paste the raw headers from a failing session?
mike: log snippet: ```
[edge] conn=42 peer=10.2.3.4 path=/v1/streams chat token=acct-xxx status=204
headers: Host: api.redwood.ai
         X-Proxy-Keepalive: 1
         Last-Event-ID: 0-175
         Content-Type: text/event-stream
```
katie: interesting that `Content-Type` is event-stream yet status=204. 204 should have no body per RFC, some browsers treat it as an EOF.
anya: that mismatch explains client behavior. some mobile SDKs close on non-2xx-with-body. but why would proxy send 204? sidecar responds early to a flush?
shrey: reproduced locally with a gap in the backend: if runtime returns `:keepalive` ping with no event payload, our proxy normalizes to 204 to save bytes. that was an optimization to avoid chunked delimiters.
mike: so optimization breaks resume idempotency -> double-charge. rollouts flagged this in the console?
deploy-bot: Canary deployment 423 -> eu-edge v2 deployed at 1769999940, 12% traffic.
anya: we need to stop sending 204 for active SSE clients. quick mitigation: have proxy transform 204 -> 200 with a tiny comment event `:keepalive

` so browsers/SDKs won't close. low-risk and reversible.
katie: telemetry change: console should surface `keepalive_status_code_override` metric so we can track how often proxy rewrites 204->200.
mike: also need to avoid double-billing: add resume dedupe by resume-id + last-event-id within a 10s window at billing collector. fallback even if we fix proxy.
shrey: agree. I'll open two PRs: (1) proxy: disable 204 normalization and emit comment keepalive, (2) billing: dedupe resume by (tenant,resume_id,last_event_id) TTL 10s.
anya: pinging @katie for console UX: where should the metric surface? route-level alerts or global streaming dashboard?
katie: route-level first, add a small badge in the streaming route overview: "Keepalive mismatches" with link to recent traces. we'll add an alert at 0.5% of requests in a minute.
mike: timeline? this is causing noticeable user reconnects for a few EU customers. can we hotfix proxy tomorrow morning?
shrey: I can hotfix the canary config tonight and promote if green. PRs in draft at https://git.redwood/s/proxy/pulls/458 and https://git.redwood/s/billing/pulls/112
anya: also update SDK docs advising that clients should treat 204 as terminal for now, but we'll aim to ensure servers never send 204 for active SSE. small note in changelog.
mike: thanks. I'll open a short incident ticket and tag customers who reported it.
katie: created dashboard panel and alert rule, ID #STR-204-KA. tagging console oncall for visibility. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
deploy-bot: Canary promotion completed to 50% at 1769999995
mike: monitoring for dup charges and reconnects now. thanks all. :thumbsup:
